name: Paddy rice
note: Staple wetland cereal. Needs standing water and warm nights; grain-filling fails above ~35C at flowering.

name: Maize
note: Warm-season cereal, base temp 10C. Drought-sensitive at tasselling; heat above 35C aborts pollen.

name: Cassava
note: Drought-hardy tropical root crop. Very wide rainfall tolerance; frost-free year-round required.

name: Groundnut
note: Legume (peanut). Tolerates heat and semi-arid conditions; waterlogging rots the pods.

name: Sweet potato
note: Tropical root crop, frost-sensitive. Reliable smallholder staple on marginal soils.

name: Soybean
note: Oilseed legume. Sensitive to heat at flowering and to both drought and waterlogging.

name: Mung bean
note: Short-cycle legume (~65 days). Heat-tolerant, good as a dry-season catch crop.

name: Sorghum
note: Drought-tolerant cereal. A leading fallback crop as conditions get hotter and drier.

name: Pearl millet
note: The most drought- and heat-hardy cereal here. Grows where sorghum and maize fail.

name: Chilli
note: High-value vegetable. Flowers drop above ~35C; needs irrigation in dry spells.

name: Pineapple
note: Tropical perennial, CAM photosynthesis so very water-efficient. No frost tolerance.

name: Banana
note: Tropical perennial needing steady moisture and warmth. Wind and cold both damage it.

name: Oil palm
note: Humid-tropic plantation perennial. Needs high rainfall spread evenly across the year.

name: Rubber
note: Humid-tropic plantation tree. Long dry spells reduce latex flow; no frost tolerance.

name: Durian
note: Tropical fruit tree, very narrow climate window. Needs high heat, high humidity, no frost.

name: Jackfruit
note: Hardy tropical fruit tree. More heat- and drought-tolerant than durian; frost-sensitive.

name: Pigeon pea
note: Deep-rooted perennial legume. Very drought-tolerant; fixes nitrogen, good for poor soils.

name: Taro
note: Wetland root crop, thrives in waterlogged soils like rice. Needs high, reliable rainfall.
